newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cerj goes on sale Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cerj goes on sale Wednesday.

text.p: Rio de Janeiro state power firm Companhia de Eletricidade do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (Cerj) is being sold off on the Rio stock exchange as scheduled November 20, the state planning department confirmed.

The state is selling off its 78 percent stake in Cerj, with 10 percent of the stake going to Cerj employees and the remaining 70.2 percent of total Cerj share capital being sold in a closed envelope auction for a minimum price of 464.7 million reais ($451.2 million).
Cerj, the first of Rio de Janeiro's state companies to be privatized, supplies 25 percent of Rio de Janeiro state's electricity and serves around 1.2 million customers.
A total of 35 Brazilian and foreign companies have prequalified for the privatization auction.

Under the privatization rules any consortium participating in the auction will have to include a power company with at least 1 million customers, sales of at least 5,000 gigawatts in 1995 and less than 12 percent energy losses.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
